harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.1.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.2.0/24) using pure routing plus stateful forward-filter firewall rules, with no NAT, so node2 and node3 reach each other on any port with original source addresses preserved. Added static routes on node2/node3 pointing at node1, and relaxed each host's local firewalld zone on the LAN NIC (it was blocking non-SSH ports, unrelated to node1's routing) so arbitrary-port TCP could be exercised end-to-end. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-id changes and post-restart functional recovery.
actions_performed: Discovered node1 has eth1/eth2 as unconfigured LAN uplinks; used test pings to determine eth1<->node2 (lan-a) and eth2<->node3 (lan-b)
Set static addresses on node1: eth1=10.50.1.254/24, eth2=10.50.2.254/24 via VyOS commit+save
Created persistent NetworkManager profiles: node2 enp8s0=10.50.1.11/24 with route to 10.50.2.0/24 via node1; node3 enp8s0=10.50.2.12/24 with route to 10.50.1.0/24 via node1
Configured VyOS firewall ipv4 forward filter: default-action drop, rule 5 accept established/related, rule 10 accept lan-a->lan-b, rule 20 accept lan-b->lan-a; confirmed no NAT rules configured
Verified net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 and per-interface forwarding=1 on node1
Adjusted firewalld zone (public->trusted) on node2/node3 LAN interface after discovering host-level firewalld blocked arbitrary TCP ports (unrelated to node1 routing)

Verified ICMP and TCP connectivity in both directions using ad-hoc HTTP listeners; tcpdump on the receiving LAN interface confirmed the original peer source IP was preserved end-to-end (no NAT rewrite)

Captured boot_id and service-state baseline on all three nodes, then sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3, polling each until reachable, confirming a changed boot_id, and re-verifying routing config, firewalld zone, and live cross-LAN connectivity after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 routes lan-a<->lan-b traffic while preserving source addresses (no NAT)
evidence.summary: VyOS 'show nat source rules' reports no NAT configured; forward-filter rules 10/20 show hit counters; tcpdump on node3's LAN interface shows node2's real IP 10.50.1.11 as the source of both ICMP and TCP traffic reaching node3, both before and after node3's restart

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
evidence.summary: Ping succeeds immediately; an arbitrary TCP port (8765) initially fails due to host firewalld default zone, is fixed by trusting the LAN interface on both nodes, then succeeds (http_code=200) in both directions (node2->node3 port 8765, node3->node2 port 9999)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered routing state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7668189d...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable then reachable with boot_id b1f8e3e4... (changed); post-restart ip_forward=1, LAN interface addresses and firewall forward-filter rules intact, and node2->node3 ping succeeds

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered LAN connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable then reachable with boot_id 5728cb31... (changed); post-restart enp8s0 address, static route to lan-b, trusted firewalld zone, and ping to node3 all confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered LAN connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bccb87ac...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable then reachable with boot_id 822352ee... (changed); post-restart enp8s0 address, static route to lan-a, trusted firewalld zone, and ping to node2 all confirmed recovered
